nodes.name: Dual-template MOF@POM self-assembly
nodes.procedure: The synthesis of MOF@POM involves a dual-template assembly process. First, a CoFeMOF (MIL-53 structure) forms through the self-coordination of Fe³⁺ and Co²⁺ with 1,4-benzenedicarboxylic acid (II), chosen for its layered structure which promotes axial growth and enhances the interaction and stability of POM-Ni-MOF stacking. This formation process is accompanied by the decomposition of symmetric PW₉-Ni₄ into a trilacunary Keggin anion, [PW₉O₃₄]⁹⁻ (PW₉). Subsequently, the CoFe-MOF reassembles with PW₉, facilitated by the Ni-O bridge, to form the innovative MOF@POM superstructure.
nodes.source_text: The synthesis of MOF@POM involves a dual-template assembly process (fig. S1). First, a CoFeMOF forms through the self-coordination of Fe³⁺ and Co²⁺ with 1,4-benzenedicarboxylic acid (II)... to form the innovative MOF@POM superstructure (Fig. 1A).

nodes.description: Water oxidation performance in three-electrode system (CV measurements)
nodes.source_text: Cyclic voltammetry (CV) measurements reveal the exceptional activity of MOF@POM for water oxidation... optimized MOF@POM demonstrates a very low overpotential of only 178 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm^{-2}... Tafel slopes... MOF@POM... 27.7 mV dec^{-1}... TOF of Co and Fe (TOF_Co+Fe) in MOF@POM is 78 times higher... mass activity of MOF@POM is >7 times greater... MOF@POM has the lowest charge-transfer resistance... electrical conductivity of MOF@POM is higher... negligible degradation for 1000 hours at a current density of 100 mA cm^{-2}

nodes.description: AEMWE performance and long-term stability at 25°C, 2 A/cm²
nodes.source_text: At 25°C, a current density of 1 A cm^{-2} is achieved with a cell voltage of only 1.83 V for MOF@POM... MOF@POM maintains a current density of 2 A cm^{-2} for 5140 hours with a minimal decay rate of 0.02 mV h^{-1} (AEM: Sustainion X37-50 Grade T, cathode: 20% Pt/C, electrolyte: 1 M KOH)

nodes.description: AEMWE performance under simulated real-world conditions (1 M KOH, 80°C)
nodes.source_text: under simulated real-world operation conditions (1 M KOH, 60° to 80°C), MOF@POM displays exceptional activity, achieving a current density of 2 A cm^{-2} with a very efficient cell voltage of only 1.69 V at 80°C (corresponding to an energy consumption of 4.04 kWh Nm^{-3} H_2). Increasing the cell voltage to 2.0 V enables a current density exceeding 5.5 A cm^{-2}... 1.78 V is sufficient to achieve a current density of 3 A cm^{-2}
The MOF@POM cell shows a decay rate of only 0.015 mV h^{-1} after 2000 hours of operation at 1 A cm^{-2}

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images display a petal-like morphology for MOF@POM, which exhibits a more uniform and ordered arrangement compared with the pure MOF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images display a petal-like morphology for MOF@POM (Fig. 1B), which exhibits a more uniform and ordered arrangement compared with the pure MOF (fig. S4).

properties.description: Scanning Electron Microscopy image showing nanostructured material with scale bars

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM measurements confirm monolayer thickness of 3.54 ± 0.18 nm for MOF@POM and 1.73 ± 0.17 nm for pure MOF, highlighting successful POM grafting.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) measurements confirm a monolayer thickness of 3.54 ± 0.18 nm for MOF@POM (Fig. 1C), in contrast to the pure MOF monolayer thickness of 1.73 ± 0.17 nm, highlighting the successful grafting of POM (fig. S5).

nodes.characterization_summary: Spherical aberration-corrected TEM reveals thin lamellar structures for MOF@POM.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, spherical aberration-corrected transmission electron microscopy (TEM) reveals thin lamellar structures (fig. S6).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM images with SAED patterns show crystalline facets in MOF@POM with 0.63 nm spacing, consistent with pure MOF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM (HRTEM) images, coupled with selected area electron diffraction (SAED) patterns (Fig. 1D), highlight the crystalline facets within the MOF@POM, with a crystalline spacing of 0.63 nm, consistent with the pure MOF (fig. S7).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD results corroborate the (200) and (001) facets for the MIL-53 MOF within MOF@POM superstructure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) results corroborate this observation of the (200) and (001) facets for the MIL-53 MOF (fig. S8), confirming the presence of the MOF within the MOF@POM superstructure

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR spectroscopy validates the presence of characteristic absorption peaks of PW9 within the MOF@POM superstructure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy also validates the presence of characteristic absorption peaks of PW9 within the MOF@POM superstructure (fig. S9)

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM with elemental mapping shows uniform distribution of Co, Fe, Ni, C, O, P, and W in MOF@POM superstructure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy analysis of MOF@POM, coupled with elemental mapping (fig. S11 and table S1), provides definitive evidence of the uniform distribution of Co, Fe, Ni, C, O, P, and W within the superstructure.

nodes.characterization_summary: Full-range synchrotron PDF analysis with excellent fit (R²≈0.88) confirms the MOF@POM superstructure, with peaks corresponding to specific atom pairs like O-W and O-Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Full-range synchrotron pair distribution function (PDF) analysis provides a detailed view of the atomic structure of MOF@POM (fig. S12). Further validation is achieved by fitting the PDF data to a structural model based on Fig. 1A. This fit shows excellent agreement (R²≈0.88) with the experimental results

nodes.characterization_summary: Thermogravimetric analysis shows POM enhances mass retention of MOF@POM compared to pure MOF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Thermogravimetric analysis of MOF@POM and the pure MOF reinforce these findings. The presence of POM enhances the mass retention of the MOF (fig. S10).

nodes.characterization_summary: Partial-PDF analysis shows excellent agreement between theoretical and experimental Ni-Fe distances, supporting POM attachment through Ni sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Partial-PDF (p-PDF) analysis further characterized the MOF@POM structure. A comparison of the p-PDF results with a structural model focused on the Ni-Fe interaction (fig. S13) reveals excellent agreement between the theoretical and experimental Ni-Fe distances.
